name: changelog-entries
summary: Writes short, clear changelog entries that tell users what changed and how it affects them.
instructions:
Use this skill whenever you add or edit a changelog entry.

1. Find the project's changelog file, usually CHANGELOG.md at the repository root. If it doesn't exist, create it with an '## [Unreleased]' section at the top.
2. Put new entries under '## [Unreleased]'. Never edit sections for versions that are already released.
3. Put each entry under one of these headings, in this order: Added, Changed, Deprecated, Removed, Fixed, Security. Only include headings that have entries.
4. Write one entry per change the user can notice. Leave out internal refactors, test-only changes, CI tweaks and dependency bumps unless users see a difference.
5. Make each entry one line and one sentence. Start with a verb in the past tense, such as 'Added', 'Fixed' or 'Removed'. Describe the effect on the user, not how the code works. Good: 'Fixed login failing when the email has uppercase letters.' Bad: 'Refactored normalizeEmail in auth service.'
6. Name the feature, command, endpoint or setting that changed, exactly as users see it. Put code identifiers in backticks.
7. Mark breaking changes with 'BREAKING:' at the start of the entry, and say in the same sentence what users must do.
8. Add the issue or pull request reference at the end in parentheses, for example '(#123)', when there is one.
9. Use plain language. No jargon, no marketing words, no exclamation marks, and don't mention people, tools or AI.
10. Before you finish, reread every entry and check: Would a user who has never seen the code understand it? Is it under the right heading? Is anything duplicated?
